features.name: English Colonial Empire
features.label: English Colonial Empire
features.source: England's first foothold on the James, drawn as Virginia alone. Cliopatria puts the English colonial empire at about 1,400 km² of mainland in 1609; the drawn shape is the lower Chesapeake shore at about 4,000, which is the smallest piece that still reads at map scale.

features.name: English Colonial Empire
features.label: English Colonial Empire
features.source: Virginia and the New England settlements at Plymouth, still two separate footholds with the Dutch between them; about 4,200 km² in Cliopatria's 1622 slice.

features.name: English Colonial Empire
features.label: English Colonial Empire
features.source: Maryland's charter and the Massachusetts Bay and Connecticut settlements; Cliopatria has the mainland at about 12,000 km² in 1632 and 18,000 by 1636.

features.name: English Colonial Empire
features.label: English Colonial Empire
features.source: The Chesapeake and New England fill out to about 25,000 km² in 1640 and 32,000 by 1645.

features.name: English Colonial Empire
features.label: English Colonial Empire
features.source: The Albemarle settlements reach into Carolina; Cliopatria has about 46,000 km² in 1653 and 52,000 by 1662.

features.name: English Colonial Empire
features.label: English Colonial Empire
features.source: New Netherland surrendered in September 1664, joining the Chesapeake to New England as one seaboard for the first time.

features.name: English Colonial Empire
features.label: English Colonial Empire
features.source: Charles Town founded; Cliopatria's 1670 slice roughly doubles the mainland to about 101,000 km².

features.name: English Colonial Empire
features.label: English Colonial Empire
features.source: Pennsylvania and the inland growth of the older colonies; about 131,000 km² in 1683 and 147,000 by 1687.

features.name: British Colonial Empire
features.label: British Colonial Empire
features.source: The Acts of Union took effect on 1 May 1707. Cliopatria's British colonial empire inherits the mainland at about 152,000 km².

features.name: British Colonial Empire
features.label: British Colonial Empire
features.source: Growth inland and into Maine; Cliopatria has about 216,000 km² from its 1718 slice.

features.name: British Colonial Empire
features.label: British Colonial Empire
features.source: Georgia's charter extends the seaboard south to the Altamaha; about 229,000 km² in Cliopatria's 1734 slice.

features.name: British Colonial Empire
features.label: British Colonial Empire
features.source: The frontier moves further into the piedmont: about 289,000 km².

features.name: British Colonial Empire
features.label: British Colonial Empire
features.source: About 391,000 km² in 1752 and 416,000 by 1757, as settlement pushes toward the mountains on the eve of the Seven Years' War.

features.name: British Colonial Empire
features.label: British Colonial Empire
features.source: The Proclamation of 1763 closes the crest of the Appalachians to settlement, which is where this shape stops; Quebec and the Floridas won in the same year are drawn separately.

features.label: Rupert's Land (Britain)
features.source: The Hudson's Bay Company held its charter from 1670, but France held most of the bay until Utrecht returned it in 1713, which is where Cliopatria starts Britain in the north — about 200,000 km² in its 1713 slice against 14,000 in 1709. Drawn to Confederation-era Rupert's Land as one part.

features.label: British North America
features.source: Quebec and the maritime colonies after the Treaty of Paris, drawn with the later provincial extents.

features.label: Florida (Britain)
features.source: Britain held East and West Florida between the Treaties of Paris.

features.label: British Guiana
features.source: The Essequibo, Demerara and Berbice colonies; Britain consolidated control during the Napoleonic era.

features.name: English Colonial Empire
features.label: Newfoundland (English Colonial Empire)
features.source: The Cupids colony of 1610, the first English settlement on the island. Labrador is no longer drawn with it: that came with the Proclamation of 1763.

features.name: British Colonial Empire
features.label: Newfoundland (Britain)
features.source: A colony, then a dominion in its own right, until it voted to join Canada.

features.label: Labrador (Britain)
features.source: Annexed to Newfoundland by the Proclamation of 1763 and drawn with it after that. Kept as a span of its own so the mainland is named Labrador rather than taking the island's name, which is what a single span would do — the anchor goes to the larger piece.

features.label: Prince Edward Island (Britain)
features.source: Île Saint-Jean, ceded with Canada in 1763 and the last colony to join Confederation.

features.label: New Caledonia (Britain)
features.source: The Hudson's Bay Company took the western districts under an exclusive licence in 1821, and the Anglo-Russian convention fixed the northern line in 1825; Cliopatria's British extent in Canada only reaches past the Rockies in the 1820s. Before that the ground west of the mountains is left blank rather than drawn British.

features.label: British Columbia
features.source: The Oregon Treaty gave Britain everything north of the 49th parallel, which is when that line first belongs on the map.

features.label: British Arctic Territories
features.source: Claimed on the strength of the Parry and Ross voyages of the 1820s — Cliopatria's British reach in Canada passes 63°N in 1822 — held back at Confederation and transferred to Canada in 1880.

features.label: Belize (Britain)
features.source: A logwood settlement held in fact under Spanish and then Guatemalan sovereignty, which is why it is drawn as contested until it became the colony of British Honduras.

features.label: Trinidad (Britain)
features.source: Taken by British expedition in 1797; shown as occupied until the Treaty of Amiens confirmed British possession.

features.label: St Lucia (Britain)
features.source: Changed hands between Britain and France repeatedly until Paris confirmed it as British in 1814; drawn as British throughout.

features.label: Falkland Islands (Britain)
features.source: Britain re-established administration in 1833 and has administered the islands since.
